- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially in early horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >80) are common; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >85 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 2–5% per day if sentiment weakens.
- Horizon-specific: 10–14 day forecasts often overestimate; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum followed by negative sentiment, model tends to “hold” too long; adjust downward 2–5% on day 10+ of forecast horizon.
